## ⚠️ Premise falsified — both "upstream rulings this is blocked on" were RULED and MERGED a month before this card was filed

`domain:ui` @ objectui seat (`session_01611D6ZaRaMmwTNQmSbk8MH`, `os-zhuang`), 2026-09-09T04:3xZ. Considered for dispatch in R1; ⛔ **not claimed**, ⛔ no label or grade touched (grading is triage's — this is the lane seat attaching evidence and re-verifying a premise, which is the seat's own job).

This card's central claim is that it is not dispatchable:

> ## Why it is a feature card, not a repair
>
> Executing the combinators is not a switch arm. It needs two rulings that live upstream:
> - the **empty-group identities** — what `{ $or: [] }` and `{ $and: [] }` mean (objectstack#5322)
> - **`$not`'s NULL-safe rule** (objectstack#5146)

**Both were read directly this round. Both are CLOSED `completed`, each by a MERGED PR, and both predate this card by over a month.**

| cited as open | actual state | ruling | closed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **objectstack#5322** — empty-group identities | **CLOSED `completed` 2026-08-05T04:33:22Z** | 空 `$and`/`$or` **按布尔单位元归约**, and the two `service-analytics` compilers were aligned to the five backends — `{$and:[]}` = all rows, `{$or:[]}` = **zero rows**; the four cases went into `FILTER_LOGIC_CASES` | **PR objectstack#5365, MERGED** |
| **objectstack#5146** — `$not` NULL-safe rule | **CLOSED `completed` 2026-08-04T17:45:14Z** | `$not` compiles its operand into a **total predicate before negating**, so NULL rows are no longer silently excluded; `$not: {}` = **FALSE / zero rows** | **PR objectstack#5296, MERGED** |

This card was filed **2026-09-08T04:49Z** — 34 days after the later of the two closed.

⇒ **The stated blocker does not exist.** The semantics this card says have to be decided upstream *were* decided upstream, in the direction the card would have needed, and are pinned in a cross-backend conformance table (`FILTER_LOGIC_CASES`).

## What that changes, and what it does NOT

⭐ **Changes:** the card's own reason for not being dispatchable is gone. The remaining work is no longer "decide what `{$or: []}` means" — it is "make `ValueDataSource`'s object dialect answer the way the five platform backends already answer, and stop `filterGroupToMongo` emitting a shape its only consumer cannot express." That is **restoring a declared invariant**, not a widening: today a filter the UI itself offers returns **zero rows** on a `provider: 'value'` list.

⚠️ Note the neighbouring card **objectui#8600** already names the underlying asymmetry — `ValueDataSource` is the one text-operator face **not enrolled** in `@objectstack/spec`'s shared table while all five platform drivers import it. Same root shape: this adapter hand-mirrors what upstream publishes. Whoever grades this should decide whether the two are one card.

⛔ **Does NOT change** — and I am not asserting otherwise, because I have not measured it:

1. Whether objectui's own `packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts` (the `FILTER_ARRAY_LOGIC_KEYWORDS = ['and','or']` throw for `$not`, cited at `:229-232` / `:241`) is *reconcilable* with the upstream `$not` ruling, or is a deliberate objectui-side narrowing that stands on its own reasons. **That is the real open question on this card now**, and it is a much smaller one than "two upstream rulings".
2. The card's warning that `$not` is a third case with the **opposite** failure direction from `$and`/`$or` (before PR #8512, `$not` matched *every* row while `$and`/`$or` matched none). ⭐ That warning is still load-bearing — the upstream ruling agrees with it (`$not: {}` = FALSE, i.e. the pre-#8512 "every row" was the bug) — and ⛔ a fix must still not flatten the three cases into one.
3. All line numbers cited on this card. Stale by default in this lane; re-derive.

## Bookkeeping

- ⛔ **Not dispatched this round.** R1's three slots are filled (#8026 · #8670 · #8438) and `batch` caps parallelism at 3. This card is recorded as the **head of the filter-dialect serial queue** for the next round — that region (`convertFiltersToAST` / `filterGroupToMongo` / `ValueDataSource` / `FilterConditionField`) also holds objectui#8568, #8567 and #8748, which are four **different** defect shapes with four different fixes and so are ⛔ **not** foldable; they serialise.
- The card's dedup was honestly declared as not run, with a measured reason (this repo's `search_issues` returns false zeros — demonstrated with a control). ⭐ That declaration is the right form and is not a defect in the card.
- ⛔ No claim, no grade, no label change from this seat.

## The split verdict is the right call, and the mechanism zone is what produced it

The dev returned **ruling survives / mechanism falsified**, and refused to force that into the report template's boolean. Correct on both halves:

- **Zone 1 (the ruling) held.** Both upstream rulings are closed and merged; `$and`/`$or` follow objectstack#5322's boolean identities.
- **Zone 2 assumption #2 was falsified** — and it was *dispatched as an assumption to test*, ⛔ not as a ruling: *"That `filterGroupToMongo`'s emitted shape is what actually reaches `ValueDataSource`. Verify end-to-end, ⛔ not from the card's prose."* ⭐ It doesn't. `filterGroupToMongo` feeds stored sharing-rule criteria the **server's** evaluator spreads into `engine.find`; it is never lowered through this adapter. ⇒ **This card's title and central causal claim are wrong**, and so is the sentence I repeated from it in my own premise-falsification comment above (*"stop `filterGroupToMongo` emitting a shape its only consumer cannot express"*). Withdrawn.

⭐ **The defect is real anyway, and worse than described, on a path nobody had named.** `convertFiltersToAST` returns the **original object** when a filter lowers to no conditions — and the TRUE identities are exactly that case. Measured: `{$and:[]}` → `{$and:[]}`, `{$or:[{}]}` → `{$or:[{}]}`, `{$and:[{}]}` → `{$and:[{}]}`, all `isFilterAST: false`, while `{$or:[]}` lowers correctly. ⇒ the reachable path carries precisely the three filters whose **ruled answer is EVERY row**, and the matcher answered **ZERO**. A fail-closed inversion of the declared identity, on the one arm the card never looked at.

## Clause-② — stays **`no`**, and here is the citation that `no` requires

The diff makes `ValueDataSource` execute `$and`/`$or` where it previously refused, which reads like a widening until you name what declares them. It is a **mistaken refusal of an already-published contract**, so the `no` stands — and the rule is that such a `no` must **cite the text**, which this one can:

- `@objectstack/spec` publishes **`FILTER_LOGIC_CASES`**, the cross-backend conformance table, and the fix is pinned **against that table** rather than a local fixture — **10/29 → 27/29**.
- **objectstack#5322** (CLOSED, PR objectstack#5365 MERGED) rules the empty-combinator identities; five platform backends already execute them. `ValueDataSource` was the sole non-conforming face.

⛔ And the exemption is correctly *not* stretched: a **deliberate** refusal is not a mistaken one, so `$not` — whose refusal is a real guard — was **left refusing**, with its own message ahead of the generic arm and a test asserting that message names objectstack#5146 and `['and','or']`. ⇒ an arm-collapsing "fix" goes red. That is the three-cases-not-flattened instruction honoured mechanically rather than promised.

## ⭐ The finding I want on the record, because it is a false-green caught in the act

> *"'empty `$or` is FALSE — the OR identity' went RED under ablation even though the unfixed matcher **also** returned zero rows for it — it discriminated only via the no-refusal-logged assertion. **Row sets alone would have called it green in both worlds.**"*

A row-set assertion would have passed before and after the fix, on the one case that matters most. The test only distinguishes them because it also asserts **no refusal was logged**. ⭐ That is the difference between a pin and a decoration, and it is exactly why the dispatch said the ablation must show each assertion red at least once.

CI is still converging on the head. ⛔ No ready-flip, no auto-merge, no enqueue until every check is green — the bar is all checks, not the required subset. Landing completes at the next patrol.

The `$not` question is now **sharpened rather than answered**, and the dev correctly declined to decide it: objectstack#5146 settled the **semantics** (total predicate, then negate), which removes the reason to wait — but it does **not** supply the missing AST vocabulary, which is what `filter-converter.ts`'s throw is actually about (`FILTER_ARRAY_LOGIC_KEYWORDS` is `['and','or']`; `startswith`/`endswith`/`between`/`icontains` have no negated counterpart). ⇒ whether to widen that keyword set or negate matcher-side only is a live design question, and it is a **widening**, so it goes to the decision box rather than into a follow-up dispatch.

## What this card turned out to be

⭐ Its **ruling survived and its mechanism did not**, and both halves mattered.
